title: Freely given (Matthew 10:1–15)
hook: freely you have received, freely give
tomorrow: how do you walk among wolves and stay gentle?

segments.voice: Yesterday the field was full and the hands were few. Your line: the harvest is plentiful. Today the hands get names.
screen: `THE HARVEST IS PLENTIFUL.` → `THE HANDS GET NAMES.`

segments.voice: Free trial, then the card gets charged. Free shipping over a certain total. Free is usually a hook. Matthew uses the word another way. He stops to read out names: Simon called Peter, Andrew his brother, James and John, Matthew the publican, the tax collector from the booth, and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him. Twelve, given power to heal, and about to hear their one rule about money.
screen: `FREE TRIAL, THEN THE CHARGE.` → `THE TWELVE, BY NAME.` → `ONE RULE ABOUT MONEY.`

segments.voice: Here it is: "Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out devils: freely ye have received, freely give." The reason comes with the rule. Nothing they carry was bought, so none of it is for sale. They aren't even allowed to pack: "Provide neither gold, nor silver, nor brass in your purses." And "the workman is worthy of his meat": the givers live on what others give them. Free giving runs both ways: the people who give for nothing also receive for nothing. If a house says no, "let your peace return to you." The peace isn't wasted; it comes home. So the question underneath: what do you owe for a gift? Not a payment. A passing-on. This is shared ground with a neighbor. The Dhammapada, a collection of the Buddha's sayings, says in Max Müller's translation: "The gift of the law exceeds all gifts." Law there means the dhamma, the Buddha's teaching. Both traditions put a teaching passed on near the top of what a person can give. And one honest difference: the twelve pass on what they received from God, healing and the news that the kingdom of heaven is at hand; the Dhammapada's gift is the Buddha's own teaching, the dhamma.
screen: `FREELY YE HAVE RECEIVED.` · `NO GOLD IN YOUR PURSES.` · `PEACE RETURNS TO YOU.` · `THE DHAMMAPADA: THE GIFT OF THE LAW.` · then, large: `FREELY GIVE.`

segments.voice: Choose one thing to give away for nothing, and take the first step before the sit ends: set the book by the door, put the coat in a bag, write down whose afternoon gets your hour. No receipt and no score, just something passing from your hands.
Freely given. What the twelve carry was never bought, so none of it is for sale.
Your line: freely give. What came as a gift goes on as a gift. Go well.

howItsDone: Some Christians read Matthew 10 when sending out missionaries or volunteers, and some ministries offer their care free of charge, pointing to freely ye have received, freely give.

fork.setup: a tutor helped you through chemistry for free and won't take anything back. now a younger kid is drowning in the same class. what fits Matthew 10?
options: help the kid for free, the way you were helped.
charge the kid, since your time is worth something now.
pay your old tutor back first, then decide.
fork.reveal: freely ye have received, freely give. the gift isn't settled by paying it back; it goes on as a gift.

original.note: Greek: as a gift, without charge. Matthew 10:8 uses it for both halves: freely received, freely give.

trapdoor: what you thought: freely given means giving whatever you can spare.
what it means: the twelve give for nothing because they received for nothing, and they go out with empty purses, living on others' welcome.
what a scholar hears: dōrean, as a gift, stands in both halves of the line; the sending pairs free giving with free receiving, and even refused peace returns to the giver.
guess: given as a gift, because it was received as one
given only to those who can afford to pay
given away because it was worth nothing
recall: workers too few for the harvest
the disciples' wonder at the calm

chat.says: Pop said NO gifts. but he's given me everything. how do i even pay that back??
options: You can't, and that's the point. Freely received, freely give: hand him the tree, no score kept.
Then skip gifts. If something's freely given, the polite thing is giving nothing back.
Find the priciest gift you can. A gift should match what someone's given you.
chat.meaning: Jesus told the twelve: freely ye have received, freely give. A gift isn't a debt to settle; it goes on as a gift.

Judas Iscariot.meaning: one of the twelve, who betrayed Jesus

Dhammapada.meaning: a collection of the Buddha's sayings

Max Müller.meaning: a scholar who translated the Dhammapada into English

'No bag for the road' renders KJV 'scrip' (10:10).
